ratings.reviewer_notes: Directly reviews adipokines linking obesity, insulin resistance, and NAFLD; identifies TNF-alpha, IL-6, resistin, and adiponectin, with possible roles for leptin, visfatin, RBP4, omentin, and vaspin.
Direct review of obesity-related adipokine imbalance in NAFLD, emphasizing deficient adiponectin and excess leptin.
Provides focused evidence that PBEF/NAMPT/visfatin is elevated in NAFLD and decreases with weight loss, but states that its definite role remains unresolved.
Directly reviews dysregulated adipokine production as a mediator between obesity and NAFLD, focusing on adiponectin, adipocyte fatty acid-binding protein, and FGF-21.
NAFLD study measured leptin, adiponectin, and resistin, but the reported findings concern a CETP variant rather than adipokine associations or mechanisms.
Reviews obesity-associated leptin, adiponectin, resistin, and inflammatory cytokines, but its principal focus is progression of metabolic disease to liver cancer.

Direct longitudinal evidence in severely obese patients with NAFLD that weight loss changes systemic and hepatic adiponectin, leptin, resistin, and PBEF/NAMPT/visfatin alongside improved liver histology.
Direct review of adipokines in NAFLD/NASH pathogenesis, specifically leptin, adiponectin, resistin, TNF-alpha, and IL-6.
Randomized dietary study in adults with NAFLD showing changes in adiponectin and leptin, but it does not establish which adipokines mediate the obesity–NAFLD relationship.
HCC-focused review containing relevant NAFLD context: low adiponectin is linked to hepatic steatosis and inflammation, while leptin's role in NAFLD is described as unclear.

Review primarily addresses non-cirrhotic NAFLD-associated HCC, but identifies increased leptin and resistin and decreased adiponectin within obesity/insulin-resistance pathways promoting steatosis and inflammation.
Direct comprehensive review of adipose tissue–liver communication in obesity-related NAFLD, covering leptin, adiponectin, ghrelin, resistin, RBP4, visfatin, chemerin, and AFABP.
Direct human study in morbid obesity finding hepatic adiponectin downregulation with inflammatory liver pathology, while leptin was not associated with hepatic pathology.
Directly reviews adipocytokines released by adipose tissue as mediators of NAFLD onset and progression in obese individuals.
Direct pediatric obesity study relating adiponectin, leptin, resistin, and RBP4 to NAFLD presence, ALT activity, and ultrasonographic severity.
Mechanistic high-fat-diet mouse study showing that adiponectin deficiency worsens obesity-associated steatohepatitis and fibrosis, supporting a protective role for adiponectin.
Obese-mouse intervention improved NAFLD and altered circulating leptin, adiponectin, MCP-1, resistin, IL-6, and TNF-alpha, but did not isolate these adipokines as causal links.
Direct review identifying adiponectin, leptin, resistin, irisin, ghrelin, and visfatin as modulators of obesity-, inflammation-, and insulin-resistance-related NAFLD mechanisms.
Direct experimental study in leptin-deficient obese mice linking leptin deficiency and obesity to hepatic steatosis through increased lipogenesis and impaired mitochondrial oxidation.
Obesity-induced NASH model shows calorie restriction and resolvin D1 alter leptin, resistin, adiponectin, and inflammatory adipokines, but the primary tested mechanism is inflammatory resolution.
Direct mechanistic review of adipocytokines connecting insulin resistance and obesity to NAFLD, including adiponectin, leptin, TNF-alpha, IL-6, and resistin.
Direct human obesity study of adiponectin, leptin, and resistin; low adiponectin expression and serum levels were associated with insulin resistance and predicted NASH.
Evaluates adiponectin, leptin, resistin, and inflammatory markers for predicting NAFLD in overweight or obese adults, finding that they did not improve prediction beyond standard measures.
